newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NBNZ sees margin improvement helping 1997 result.
newsitem.headline: NBNZ sees margin improvement helping 1997 result.

text.p: The National Bank of New Zealand (NBNZ) said on Wednesday it expected improved interest margins towards the end of 1996 to flow into its 1997 result.
In a review of 1996, the worst year for the bank in five years, chairman Malcolm McCaw said tight monetary conditions and strong competition had pressured lending margins and net interest income.
Securities trading had also been down in the first half of the year, he said.
"Our net interest margin improved towards the end of the year, which means we can look forward to improved net interest income in 1997," he said.

While the bank's total assets rose NZ$1.4 billion to $16.95 billion -- driven by $1.2 billion worth of new home loans, and $400 million in new commercial and rural lending -- the bank's previously reported after-tax surplus of $97 million was well down on the $149 million reported the year before, and the lowest since 1991 when a net profit of $82 million was reported.
The return represents an after-tax return on average shareholders' equity of 10.8 percent from 17.7 percent a year earlier and a high of 22.2 percent in 1993.
Despite a 14 percent rise in the group's interest revenues to $1.713 billion, interest expenses were up 21 percent at $1.366 billion, cutting interest income by 7 percent to $374 million.

Other income was down $33 million on the year before at $226 million, with the $3 million gain from securities trading being a key component in that reduction. The year before securities trading generated a $24 million net gain.
Sales of investment securities was also down at $16 million from $50 million the year before.
Operating expenses were up $20 million at $440 million, with most of the gain rise due to higher staff costs.
At balance date the bank had total assets employed worth $16.95 billion, from $15.191 billion the year before.

Of the $13.875 billion in loans and advances, $5.557 billion was to households, with $4.26 billion to the agriculture, hunting and forestry sector, and $2.43 billion to the finance, insurance and services sector.
During the year the group wrote off $26 million in advances ($21 million previously) but recovered $2 million written off earlier.
The group's result was trimmed by $3 million charge to the group's bad and doubtful debt provision, down from $12 million the year before.
